offence_severity: Death sentence - Mitigating and aggravating circumstances
physical_harm: Injuries on the body of the deceased by way of bite marks and insertion of rod in her private parts that, inter alia, caused perforation of her intestine which caused sepsis and, ultimately, led to her death
number_of_offences: Six persons charged and finally upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the accused formed an agreement to commit heinous offences against the victim
motive: The motive was to ravish her as they liked, treat her as they felt and satisfy their gross sadistic and beastly instinctual pleasures
key_evidence_accepted: The chain of events described by the prosecutrix in her dying declarations coupled with the testimonies of the other witnesses clearly established that as soon as the informant and the prosecutrix boarded the bus, the accused persons formed an agreement to commit heinous offences against the victim.
witness_credibility: The evidence of PW-1 was unimpeachable in character and the roving cross-examination did not erode his credibility. The injuries found on the person of PW-I lent assurance to his testimony that he was present at the time of the occurrence along with the prosecutrix.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction, High Court: Affirmed, Supreme Court: Affirmed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons formed a conspiracy to commit heinous offences against the victim, including gang rape, insertion of an iron rod in her private parts, and throwing her out of a moving bus, leading to her death. The evidence established that the accused acted in concert, and the criminal acts were part of a conspiracy that resulted in the victim's death.
defence_argument: The defence highlighted mitigating factors such as the accused's background, their young age, the suffering their families would endure, and their conduct in custody. They also claimed that the accused were not hardened criminals and that the death sentence was excessive given the circumstances.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle of joint liability under Section 376(2)(g) of the Penal Code, emphasizing that all accused involved in a conspiracy or joint criminal act are liable for the entire offence, regardless of who committed the specific act.
precedent_relied_upon: Machhi Singh (Supra), Gurvail Singh@ Gala and Amr v. State of Punjab (2013) 2 SCC 713, Mohfil Khan and Anr. v. State of Jharkhand (2015) 1 SCC 67, Pumslwttam Dashrath Borate and Anr. v. State of Maharashtra (2015) 6 SCC 652
sentencing_rationale: The death sentence was imposed because the aggravating circumstances, including the brutal and diabolic nature of the crime, the coldness with which the victims were treated, and the shock to the collective conscience of society, outweighed the mitigating factors. The court held that the case fell under the 'rarest of rare' category, where no other punishment was suitable.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered the accused's background, their young age, the suffering their families would endure, their conduct in custody, and the possibility of reformation.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court weighed the brutal, diabolic nature of the crime, the insertion of an iron rod in the victim's private parts, the coldness with which the victims were thrown out of the bus, and the shock to the collective conscience of society.
